title: Cloud services & responsibility
summary: Know what the provider manages and what you manage.

passages.heading: The core idea
passages.markdown: Cloud services offer computing resources through a service model. With infrastructure as a service, the customer commonly manages guest operating systems and applications on provider-managed infrastructure. Platform as a service supplies a managed application platform so developers focus on their code and data. Software as a service delivers an application for users to configure and use. Moving to a higher-level service changes responsibilities; it does not eliminate the customer’s responsibility for access and data.

passages.heading: In the real world
passages.markdown: A public cloud offers provider-operated resources to many customers. A private cloud is dedicated to one organization, and a hybrid approach connects different environments. Elasticity means capacity can expand and contract with demand, while metered utilization measures resource consumption for management or billing. Shared physical infrastructure does not mean customers intentionally share permissions to each other’s data. Compare availability needs, data location, network connectivity, and ongoing charges before choosing a deployment. File synchronization is convenient, but deletions can synchronize too, so preserve recovery options.

passages.heading: Make it stick
passages.markdown: Put it into practice by explaining the decision in your own words. In a support scenario, identify the requirement first, connect it to the relevant technology, and check the result against that requirement. If the evidence changes, revisit your reasoning rather than repeating the same action. Document what you observed so the next person can understand your conclusion.
